content: Magnesium chloride is an electrolyte that has been approved by the FDA for use as an electrolyte replenisher in cases of magnesium deficiency. Common adverse reactions associated with its use include flushing, sweating, a significant drop in blood pressure, hypothermia, stupor, and, in severe cases, respiratory depression. For adult patients, magnesium chloride is indicated as an electrolyte replenisher in magnesium deficiencies. When administered intravenously, the recommended dosage is 4 grams diluted in 250 mL of 5% Dextrose Injection, infused at a rate not exceeding 3 mL per minute. Serum magnesium levels should be monitored to guide continued dosing. The usual dosage range is between 1 and 40 grams daily. Parenteral drug products should be visually inspected for particulate matter and discoloration prior to administration whenever the solution and container permit. There is limited information regarding off-label uses of magnesium chloride in adult patients, whether supported by guidelines or not. Similarly, there is limited information on its FDA-labeled or off-label use in pediatric patients. Magnesium chloride injection is contraindicated in patients with renal impairment, significant myocardial disease, or those in a comatose state. It should not be used if a precipitate is present in the solution. This product contains aluminum, which can be toxic, particularly in patients with impaired kidney function or in premature neonates with immature kidneys. Prolonged parenteral administration of aluminum-containing solutions can lead to central nervous system and bone toxicity, especially if aluminum levels exceed 4 to 5 mcg/kg/day. Adverse reactions reported post-marketing include flushing, sweating, a sharp drop in blood pressure, hypothermia, stupor, and respiratory depression. There is limited information available regarding drug interactions, monitoring, IV compatibility, and overdose management for magnesium chloride. In cases of suspected overdose, contacting the National Poison Help hotline is recommended. Magnesium chloride is classified as Pregnancy Category C by the FDA, meaning that animal reproduction studies have not been conducted, and it is not known whether the drug can cause fetal harm or affect reproductive capacity. It should only be administered to pregnant women if clearly needed. There is no FDA guidance on its use during labor and delivery, in nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, or specific gender or racial populations. Additionally, there is no guidance on its use in patients with renal or hepatic impairment, or in immunocompromised individuals. The mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of magnesium chloride are not well-documented in the drug label. Clinical studies on magnesium chloride are also limited. Magnesium chloride injection is supplied as a 200 mg/mL (20% w/v) solution in 50 mL multiple-dose vials. It should be stored at 20°C to 25°C (68°F to 77°F), with excursions permitted between 15°C and 30°C (59°F to 86°F). There is no established interaction between alcohol and magnesium chloride, but patients are advised to consult their doctor regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while taking this medication. The brand name for magnesium chloride is MAGNESIUM CHLORIDE®, and there is limited information on look-alike drug names.
